findings.title: No overall deadline: sequential probes make worst-case latency N x timeout_seconds
findings.evidence: checks loop calls _run_probe sequentially per name with the same timeout_seconds, so with 3 probes each hitting the 2.0s limit the endpoint blocks ~6s
findings.recommendation: Treat timeout_seconds as a total budget: compute a deadline (time.monotonic() + timeout_seconds) once, pass each probe the remaining budget (max(0, deadline - now)), and skip/mark remaining probes as down/timeout once the budget is exhausted. Alternatively document and cap the aggregate (timeout_seconds / len(probes) per probe).

findings.title: socket.create_connection timeout does not cover DNS resolution
findings.evidence: socket.create_connection is given timeout=timeout, but getaddrinfo runs before the socket timeout applies and blocks the probe past the budget
findings.recommendation: Resolve the host under the same deadline (e.g. run getaddrinfo in a worker with a bounded wait, or accept pre-resolved addresses) so a slow/hanging resolver cannot stall the health endpoint; at minimum document that the timeout only bounds connect().

findings.title: Core-ness keyed on hardcoded probe names with no validation
findings.evidence: core_down checks membership in CORE_PROBES, so a deployment naming its DB probe e.g. postgres or primary never triggers 503 when the database is down
findings.recommendation: Let callers declare which probes are core (e.g. healthcheck(probes, core_probes=CORE_PROBES) or a per-probe core flag) and fail fast (ValueError/key error in payload) when a required core probe is missing from probes.

findings.title: Empty or non-core-only probe set reports healthy 200
findings.evidence: any_down and core_down are both False for an empty probes mapping, so the function returns 200 with status ok and no checks
findings.evidence_quote: any_down = any(check["status"] == "down" for check in checks)
findings.recommendation: Guard against an empty probes mapping (raise ValueError, or return 503/down with an empty checks list) so a configuration load failure cannot masquerade as a healthy instance.

findings.title: requests float timeout applies to connect and read separately
findings.evidence: a single float is passed to http_get, which requests interprets as separate connect and read timeouts, allowing up to 2x timeout per HTTP probe
findings.recommendation: Pass a (connect, read) tuple derived from the remaining budget, or document that the effective per-probe ceiling is twice the configured value.

findings.title: No tests for the down/degraded/ok branching or probe factories
findings.evidence: the diff adds healthcheck and both probe factories with no accompanying test module, and no test command was run
findings.recommendation: Add unit tests using the http_get injection point and a fake tcp probe: core down returns 503, non-core down returns 200 degraded, all-ok returns 200 ok, probe raising is recorded as down with the exception type, and timeout_seconds <= 0 raises.
